description:
Schloss Fuschl was built around 1450 by the prince-archbishops of Salzburg as a hunting lodge, on a peninsula at the western end of Lake Fuschl, a glacial lake in the Salzkammergut. When the prince-archbishopric was dissolved in 1816 the property passed to the Austrian state.

By the 1930s the castle belonged to Gustav Edler von Remiz, a supporter of the Fatherland Front, who was imprisoned by the Nazis in Dachau and died there in 1939. His property was confiscated, and the castle became the summer residence of the Nazi foreign minister Joachim von Ribbentrop, who used it for diplomatic receptions.

It opened as a hotel in the 1950s (Rosewood gives 1954). Parts of the Sissi films starring Romy Schneider were shot here, and the estate holds a small museum of objects from the films and a collection of old master paintings. After a renovation that began in 2022, the hotel reopened on 1 July 2024 as Rosewood Schloss Fuschl, with a spa, indoor and outdoor pools and a lakeside setting about 16 km east of Salzburg.
history: Schloss Fuschl was built around 1450 by the prince-archbishops of Salzburg as a hunting lodge on a peninsula at the western end of Lake Fuschl. After the prince-archbishopric was dissolved in 1816 it passed to the Austrian state. In the 1930s it belonged to Gustav Edler von Remiz, a supporter of the Fatherland Front, who died in Dachau in 1939 after the Nazis imprisoned him; the castle was confiscated and became the summer residence of the Nazi foreign minister Joachim von Ribbentrop. It opened as a hotel in the 1950s, and parts of the Sissi films with Romy Schneider were shot here. After a renovation that began in 2022, it reopened in July 2024 as Rosewood Schloss Fuschl.

faqs.question: Was Sissi filmed at Schloss Fuschl?
faqs.answer: Yes, parts of the Sissi films starring Romy Schneider were shot at the castle, and the estate has a small museum of objects from the films.

faqs.question: How old is Schloss Fuschl?
faqs.answer: It was built around 1450 as a hunting lodge for the prince-archbishops of Salzburg and has been a hotel since the 1950s; it reopened as Rosewood Schloss Fuschl in July 2024.

meta_description: Stay at Fuschl Castle on Lake Fuschl near Salzburg, Austria — a five-star lakeside castle resort with a spa and pools. From approx. €680/night.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms and suites are spread across the castle and other buildings on the lakeside estate, including chalets; ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The castle stands on a peninsula at the western end of Lake Fuschl, in the municipality of Hof bei Salzburg, about 16 km east of Salzburg. Booking lists parking at the hotel; check whether it is charged.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €680/night for a 31 m² Deluxe Room with a king bed, air conditioning, a private bathroom, a minibar and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast and unlimited spa access included on the non-refundable rate seen; a free-cancellation rate was around €800, and a Premier Lakeside Room around €765. Booking showed a member price that is not included here, and a small tax charge (about €7) separately.

**On-site:** A spa and wellness centre, restaurants, indoor and outdoor pools including an infinity pool, a private lakeside beach and free Wi-Fi; pets are welcome, with possible fees.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one January 2027 night, a low-season date, so check your own dates on Booking. Rooms are spread across the castle and other buildings on the estate, so ask which building your room is in. The hotel reopened in July 2024 after a full renovation, so older reviews and photos may show the previous hotel.

**Combine with:** [Hohensalzburg Fortress](/castles/austria/hohensalzburg-fortress), above Salzburg's old town about 16 km to the west.
